text:
amanda: seeing DNS timeouts from eu-west GPU nodes to internal svc names (.svc.cluster.local) starting ~07:40 UTC. pod exec curl to service-ip times out, but curl to public IP works. Any recent egress/firewall changes? :eyes:
raj: saw a few alerts for nodepool-b healthcheck failures, but thought it was transient. Can you paste resolv.conf from an affected node?
amanda: pasted from one of the nodes:
```
# /etc/resolv.conf
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options edns0 trust-ad ndots:5
search default.svc.cluster.local svc.cluster.local cluster.local
```
`pod` /etc/resolv.conf shows `nameserver 10.96.0.10` though.
linus: that's interesting — host using systemd-resolved (127.0.0.53) forwarding to node-local DNS, while pods talk to cluster DNS. Could be split-horizon or node-local cache mismatch.
marie: also noticed elevated UDP fragmentation/EDNS0 errors in firewall logs around the same time. Some egress NAT boxes silently dropped large DNS responses. If EDNS0 responses get dropped, resolvers can retry TCP which we block, causing timeouts.
amanda: example dig from pod vs host:
```
# from pod
dig +short my-svc.ns.svc.cluster.local @10.96.0.10
<no response, timeout>

# from host
dig +short my-svc.ns.svc.cluster.local @127.0.0.53
<short answer> 10.244.3.12
```
linus: so host can resolve via node-local cache but pod->cluster-dns failing. That points to kube-proxy/iptables NAT or coredns forwarding issues. Any recent CoreDNS restarts?
raj: kube-system coredns pods are Running, but one node-local-dns daemonset pod on node-7 is CrashLoopBackOff in the logs around 07:38. ops-oncall, any rollback or config pushes?
ops-oncall: we pushed an iptables rule tweak to node egress chains at 07:35 to address a different NAT hole. Reverting on one test node made pod DNS start working again. Rolling back cluster-wide now. :thumbsup:
marie: rolling back is fine, but we still need a root cause doc. Hypothesis: the tweak changed the conntrack or MASQUERADE rules so that UDP/53 replies to pod IPs were not DNATed back correctly, while host-local resolvers (127.0.0.53) worked because they bypassed that path.
amanda: quick mitigation we did: restarted node-local-dns daemonset on affected nodes and added a short iptables rule to ACCEPT established,related for udp dport 53. That restored resolution for most pods.
linus: long term fixes:
- revert the iptables change and apply a test plan for NAT rule ordering
- add e2e test that queries cluster DNS from a pod and host after iptables changes
- reduce EDNS0 UDP size or allow TCP fallback through egress firewall
- add metric for node-local-dns cache hit/miss and CoreDNS upstream failures

raj: also consider switching affected host resolver to forward directly to cluster DNS IP instead of systemd-resolved stub, so host and pod path are more similar for debugging.
ops-oncall: rollback complete cluster-wide at 08:05 UTC, monitoring. If anyone sees further failures, tag #eng-infra and @ops-oncall. Incident log will be written.
sre-bot: incident created: INC-2025-0421 - DNS resolution failures on eu-west nodepool-b (links: https://internal.inc/INC-2025-0421).
amanda: thanks all — will follow up with a short postmortem and add a firewall rule test to the change checklist.
